skill.name: setup-pre-commit
skill.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged, Prettier, type checking, and tests in a JavaScript or TypeScript repository.
skill.summary: Configures Husky, lint-staged, Prettier, tests, and type checks for commit-time validation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks or fenced examples, not Ruby backtick execution. The skill still directs agents to install packages, run npx and npm commands, create a Git hook, and commit changed files. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before installing dependencies, running npx commands, or enabling npm scripts in the hook.
Specify trusted package versions or tell users to review resolved versions before installation.
Stage only generated hook and configuration files, then show git status before committing.

content.value_statement: Manual hook setup is easy to miss across package managers. This skill guides Husky, lint-staged, Prettier, tests, and type checks in one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Detects npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun from lockfiles.
Installs Husky, lint-staged, and Prettier as development dependencies.
Initializes Husky and creates the pre-commit hook.
Configures lint-staged to run Prettier on staged files.
Adds a default Prettier configuration when none exists.
Verifies hook files, package scripts, and lint-staged execution.
limitations: Targets JavaScript and TypeScript projects with package.json.
Relies on package manager commands and installed npm packages.
Omits typecheck or test commands when scripts are missing.
Does not design custom lint, test, or formatting rules.

use_cases.title: New JavaScript Project
use_cases.description: Add a standard pre-commit workflow before the repository grows.

use_cases.title: Team Commit Standards
use_cases.description: Create consistent formatting, test, and typecheck gates for contributors.

use_cases.title: Repository Cleanup
use_cases.description: Add missing hook automation to an existing package-based project.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks in this repository. Use the detected package manager and add lint-staged with Prettier.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the project has no existing hook setup.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Existing Scripts
prompt_templates.prompt: Add pre-commit hooks, but keep existing package scripts unchanged. Omit typecheck or test commands if scripts are absent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when script safety matters more than full coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Package Manager Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up pre-commit hooks using pnpm. Configure lint-staged, Prettier, and Husky without replacing existing formatting settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the package manager is already known.

prompt_templates.title: Audit And Integrate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository, detect existing hook or formatter configuration, then add a minimal Husky and lint-staged workflow with verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for mature repositories with existing tooling.

output_examples.input: Please add pre-commit formatting to this npm project.
output_examples.output: The assistant detects npm, installs the needed development dependencies, initializes Husky, configures lint-staged, and summarizes verification results.

output_examples.input: This repo already has tests but no typecheck script.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds formatting and test checks to the hook, omits the missing typecheck command, and explains the omission.

output_examples.input: Set this up without changing my existing Prettier rules.
output_examples.output: The assistant preserves the existing formatter configuration, adds the hook workflow, and reports the files changed.

best_practices: Review package.json scripts before enabling them in a commit hook.
Run lint-staged manually before committing the generated hook files.
Inspect staged files before using the final commit instruction.
anti_patterns: Running the setup in a repository with unresolved package manager conflicts.
Committing all changed files without reviewing generated and unrelated changes.
Adding typecheck or test commands when the repository has no matching scripts.

faq.question: Which package managers can it detect?
faq.answer: It checks for npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun lockfiles, then uses the matching package manager.

faq.question: Does it create a Prettier config?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates a default Prettier config only when no existing Prettier config is present.

faq.question: Will it always run tests before commit?
faq.answer: No. It adds test and typecheck commands only when matching package scripts exist.

faq.question: Can it work with existing Husky hooks?
faq.answer: It can guide setup, but existing hooks should be reviewed before changes are made.

faq.question: Does it install packages?
faq.answer: Yes. It installs Husky, lint-staged, and Prettier as development dependencies.

faq.question: Is it safe to use in any repository?
faq.answer: Use it after reviewing commands and staged files because it modifies hooks and package configuration.
